messages:
sophie: Flagging urgent: several customers reported bulk deprovisions from SCIM overnight. We have ~1200 deprov events in a 10m window tied to the provisioning service. Not a normal pattern.

devin: Any error in the provisioning logs? 401/403/429?

sophie: Main error is `introspection_failed` with 401 and `invalid_token` on the introspection call to idp.prod. See log snippet: `POST /introspect -> 401 {\"error\":\"invalid_client\"}`

maria-platform: provisioning treats an introspect failure as token invalid -> triggers deprovision for service-account mapped users. That behavior is intentional but we should stop mass deprovs until root cause known. Can we pause the deprov worker?

linda-ops: pausing deprov queue now (job: pause-scim-deprovs-564). Deploy-bot: job queued.

deploy-bot: job started: pause-scim-deprovs-564 -> 1759999028

devin: good. Next: why introspection 401? Usually client cert or client_secret issue. We recently rotated the introspection client certificate in KMS last night as part of key hygiene. Linda, did that touch the client cert secret or mount for prod?

linda-ops: yes we rotated certs per schedule (rotate-certs-2026-05-03). The rotation uploaded a new cert bundle to secret manager and updated the rotation-annotation service config. I verified the cert chain but not the secret version binding.

henry-sec: check if provisioning service did a hot reload of the client cert; also check CA trust. If introspection server requires mTLS, a wrong client cert (expired or missing SAN) will lead to 401/invalid_client.

maria-platform: I ran `curl --cert client.pem --key client.key https://idp.prod.example.com/introspect -d 'token=...' -v` from staging host and got `SSL: certificate subject mismatch` locally but prod logs show 401, not TLS-level failure. Could be that our proxy terminates TLS and forwards without client cert.

devin: can you dump the client cert fingerprint used by the provisioning service? `openssl x509 -in /etc/provisioner/client.pem -noout -fingerprint`

sophie: grabbing fingerprint now from a failing host: `SHA1 Fingerprint=AB:CD:12:34:56:78:90:EF:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:AA:BB:CC`

linda-ops: the rotation job mistakenly bumped the secret reference to version `projects/redwood/secrets/idp-introspect-cert/versions/999` which is a placeholder/expired cert used in staging. Oops — prod ended up with staging cert. Ill revert to previous secret version.

deploy-bot: start deploy job revert-introspect-cert-770 -> 1759999065

devin: while revert runs, we should: 1) check KMS audit for the rotation call, 2) confirm the active secret version, 3) ensure no other services picked up the placeholder cert. Henry, can you check KMS audit?

henry-sec: running `gcloud logging read "resource.type=secretmanager AND protoPayload.methodName=\"v1.SecretManagerService.UpdateSecret\"" --limit 50` now. Found the rotate job triggered by ops-service-account at 1759998550 and it updated secret `idp-introspect-cert` to version 999. No other writes found.

maria-platform: revert succeeded per deploy-bot: revert-introspect-cert-770 -> 1759999098

linda-ops: after revert I restarted the provisioner (rolling restart). Provisioner logs now show introspect 200 for sampled tokens. SCIM worker remains paused until we validate.

sophie: quick verification: ran intropsect call from provisioner host -> `200 {"active":true}`. Good. Now need to reconcile the ~1200 deprovs. Is there a partial rollback plan?

maria-platform: we have the audit records and SCIM events. We can queue re-provision jobs for affected accounts but must confirm no manual RBAC changes happened concurrently. Sophie, do you have RBAC audit for last 2h?

sophie: RBAC audit shows a role update at 1759995000 that removed `scim:write` from a role, but that rollout targeted a non-provisioning principal. So likely unrelated. The timing aligns with the cert rotation though.

\enherry-sec: action items: (1) re-run reprovision for impacted accounts from backups (2) add a safety gate to never perform mass deprovision if introspection errors spike above threshold, (3) add a preflight step in rotation job to verify secret version exists and is not in the staging allowlist, (4) add an alert for secret version changes for idp-introspect-cert.

audit-bot: create alert: secret-change idp-introspect-cert -> pager (owner=eng-security)

linda-ops: noted. Ill update rotation job to validate `secret.metadata.labels.environment == prod` and to fail fast. Also pausing scheduled cert rotations until we have canary tests.

sophie: Ill start a re-provision job for the affected customers and coordinate with support to notify impacted accounts. Will publish a short incident note.

devin: please include timeline and the exact secret version changes in the PM. Also add a quick fix doc for provisioning to avoid auto-deprov on transient introspection failures (circuit breaker).

sophie: will do. Closing once reprovision completed and postmortem published.
